copy.blurb:
Ecuador face Germany on Thursday, evening UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — a wide disagreement by the engine's standards on the Ecuador side, +10.1pp.

Public Elo rates Germany 110 points higher than the other side (Ecuador 1790, Germany 1900). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Ecuador to win at 27%, the draw at 23%, and Germany to win at 50%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Ecuador on the win side reads 27%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Ecuador to win at 16%, the draw at 22%, and Germany to win at 62%. The Ecuador side trades at 16% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +506. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 27%, +10.1pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Ecuador side that lower bound is 23% — +6.0pp clear of the market's 16%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 34 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade. Two outlets covered the build-up this week — BBC Sport (football): "Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer comes out of international retirement to be named in Germany's squad for the 2026 World Cup, with…"; The Guardian (football): "Yes I plan with [Neuer as No 1]"
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Ecuador a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +10.1pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

editorial_citations.quote: Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer comes out of international retirement to be named in Germany's squad for the 2026 World Cup, with manager Julian Nagelsmann saying the 40-year-old will be his team's number one for the tournament.
Yes I plan with [Neuer as No 1]
The main task was to nominate the best three keepers. So we decided that these three are part of that. We contacted Manuel and asked him if he wanted to play for the national team again.

copy.summary: The model thinks Ecuador are mispriced. Our number reads 27% on the home side; the market reads 16%. The +10.1pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Ecuador v Germany · the model leans Ecuador
